gauntlet: question
Before the first question, I need to correct a premise from the gathered draft. The draft says the existing settings resolver cannot accept overrides, but primary code disproves that: `settings/resolver.ts:11` already accepts a timeout override. I also traced the callers and found that every one of them reads settings through that resolver, so no consumer needs a second path. The missing timeout override appears to come from the affected caller not passing its override into the resolver, not from a gap in the resolver itself. I'll continue the design on this corrected fact unless you override it. I'll record it, and any override, in the draft for `## Problem`.

This means a second settings file would add a parallel boundary beside the resolver that already owns every setting. It would also leave the actual cause in place. No ticket decision settles this point, so I need your call on the framing:

A) as framed - add a second settings file that supplies the timeout override
B) pivot: change the existing caller to pass its timeout override through `settings/resolver.ts:11` - this fixes the root cause on the one read path every caller already uses
C) smaller or none: document how to pass the override through the existing resolver and ship no code change; the missing override stays until a caller is updated
Recommendation: B - the resolver already supports the override and owns every setting, so fixing the caller removes the bug without duplicating the settings boundary.

The draft’s claim that the existing resolver cannot accept overrides is disproved: `settings/resolver.ts:11` already accepts a timeout override, and primary-code recon confirmed every caller uses that resolver. A second settings file would duplicate the existing settings boundary; passing the override from the existing caller addresses the root cause.

Which direction should we take?
A) as framed — add a second settings file.
B) pivot: pass the timeout override through the existing caller — the shared resolver already supports it.
C) smaller or none: leave the timeout behavior unchanged and add no settings file.
Recommendation: B - fixes the missing override through the boundary every caller already uses.
